entities.summary:
Master Paul of Levoča was a renowned medieval carver and sculptor of the 15th and 16th century, active primarily in the Carpathian-German town of Levoča, Slovakia.

Born in 1480 to a family of modest means, Master Paul's exceptional artistic talent was evident from an early age, drawing the attention of local patrons and nobles.

His most notable works include the intricately carved altarpiece for the Levoča parish church and the majestic frescoes adorning the ceiling of the town's town hall.

Master Paul's legacy extends beyond his individual masterpieces, as he played a pivotal role in shaping the artistic identity of the Carpathian-German region.
